articles.title: In a streaming wars world, JustWatch has become an essential tool
articles.summary: With the ever-increasing number of different streaming services and shifting rights battles, JustWatch — a search engine that tells you where any show or movie is available to stream — has become an essential tool for navigating the streaming wars.
articles.body: There are too many streaming services, and all of them are fighting over content that feels like it’s bouncing back and forth between streaming sites on a daily basis. This has made sites like JustWatch — a streaming search engine and recommendation site — an essential tool as more and more of these services continue to launch. JustWatch isn’t a new service; it’s been around since 2014. But the modern-day glut of streaming services and spiraling rights agreements have made it more essential than ever. At its core, JustWatch is a search engine for digital media. Type in a movie or TV show, and it’ll tell you everywhere you can stream it, watch it for free with ads, buy, or rent it. Once you’ve found what you’re looking for, you simply click and it’ll link you directly to that service. It’s not the only site or app that does this, but I’ve found it to be far and away the most reliable and useful. And that’s for a few reasons. The first is simply how comprehensive JustWatch is. It loops in basically every streaming service and TV show / movie seller under the sun — even ones that I had forgotten existed. Did I remember that CW Seed is a real website? Absolutely not, but it turns out it’s the only place you can currently stream the criminally underrated Pushing Daisies, something that I only learned from checking JustWatch. The site is also super up to date. HBO Max, for example, was already showing up in JustWatch results on the first day it was available. And seemingly no service is too obscure for JustWatch: it even has Quibi shows! [Image: But what sets it above and beyond the rest is that you can also filter searches based on specific streaming services. Only subscribe to Hulu and Netflix? Your search results will only show those services, if you want. You can also use more advanced filters, sorting by just movies or TV shows, IMDB rating, or MPAA age ratings, too. Only interested in 4K? JustWatch can tell you if it’s available or not. And if the movie you want isn’t available to stream somewhere, JustWatch also shows prices from basically every major retailer for renting or buying a film digitally. That’s extremely useful for comparing prices, whether you’re interested in building out your own digital library or just want the cheapest place to rent Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure this weekend. JustWatch isn’t just limited to US services: it’s available in over 45 countries around the world, including Canada and the United Kingdom. That makes it crucial in the streaming wars because what content is available, where it’s streaming, and even which services are available can shift wildly depending on what country you’re in. (For example, Star Trek: Discovery is a CBS All Access exclusive in the US, but available on Netflix in the UK.) With streaming catalogs continuing to shift and change over the coming months and years (just ask WarnerMedia, which has already had to amend HBO Max advertisements to note some movies will soon be leaving the service or aren’t available yet), finding who has the rights to the movie you want to watch is only going to get more difficult. And while nothing short of shifting market forces is likely to change that anytime soon, at least there are services like JustWatch to help sort out the chaos.

articles.title: Elgato won over creators — its new Neo line is for everyone else
articles.summary: Elgato is launching a Neo line of products that aren’t all about gaming or streaming. A new webcam, microphone, and Stream Deck are targeted at everyone.
articles.body: If you watch a Twitch streamer, it’s almost guaranteed that they will be using at least one Elgato product. After dominating this part of the market for years, Elgato is now shifting its primary focus away from gaming with its new Neo line while also preparing a bevy of AI features to improve new and existing gear. Neo is a collection of Elgato’s most popular products made simpler, more affordable, and more compact so they can be used easily with a laptop or iPad. “They look more accessible, they look more friendly,” says Julian Fest, general manager of Elgato, in an interview with The Verge. “The entire industrial design is focused on being more appealing to a less technical audience.” The $99.99 Stream Deck Neo is the star of the show, essentially the command center for Elgato’s products. It has eight LCD keys that can be paired to automate tasks like turning on lights or joining video calls. I use Stream Deck buttons to mute myself on calls, pause my notifications in Slack, and see what music is playing on Spotify. Elgato has added two capacitive buttons to let you switch pages for an infinite amount of customizable keys. There’s also an info display between these buttons that acts like a digital clock that’s always available. [Image: The Stream Deck Neo is small enough for laptop use. Neo is Elgato’s way of bringing its expertise in streaming to the masses — an acknowledgment that the line between creator and professional is increasingly blurred as more and more people dial into meetings remotely. But it’s also an admission that setting up webcams, lights, and microphones isn’t an easy task for most people. “We want the out-of-box experience to be quite seamless,” says Fest. Elgato’s Neo line is designed to be plug-and-play so you can quickly and easily improve your setup without having to install multiple apps and tweak settings. Elgato is trying to appeal to people who are looking for something in between a basic webcam / microphone combination and the more high-end audio and video setup it’s typically known for. [Image: The Wave Neo microphone and Game Capture Neo. The lineup includes key hardware for video calls. The $99.99 Facecam Neo webcam supports 1080p video at 60fps, includes an integrated privacy shutter, and can easily slot onto the top of a monitor or your laptop. The $89.99 Wave Neo condenser microphone has a raised desktop stand and a tap-to-mute feature and will also integrate into Elgato’s more advanced Wave Link app. If you need better lighting at your desk or on the go, the $89.99 Key Light Neo is a diffused light that’s designed to pair with a webcam. While Elgato’s other Key Lights have typically shipped with stands, the Key Light Neo can be mounted to the top of a laptop or a monitor so it doesn’t take up any desk space. It has up to 800 lumens of brightness, and there are controls at the front to adjust the brightness and color temperature. The $119.99 Game Capture Neo is still very much rooted in the history of Elgato products aimed at streamers and gamers. You can use it to capture video from a PlayStation, Xbox, or Nintendo Switch, and it also includes pass-through support of up to 4K / 60fps with HDR enabled. Game Capture Neo supports capture at up to 1080p 60fps, so it’s ideal for Twitch or YouTube streaming. It’s designed to work out of the box with Discord, OBS Studio, and other apps for streaming to Twitch, YouTube, and TikTok. All of these Neo devices are available to order today, with the exception of the Facecam Neo webcam. Elgato says it’s making “further fine tuning” to the out of box experience, and expects to launch Facecam Neo in May or June. [Image: The Neo products have packaging that you can easily recycle instead of plastic. “It’s the start of a longer-term mission where we’re really trying to make more people aware that even if you don’t consider yourself a content creator, in many ways you are,” says Fest. Elgato is targeting people participating in online sales, video podcasts, events, product demonstrations, community building, and other areas where audio and visual content has been growing in recent years. “Neo really is a bet that this trend is going to keep accelerating,” says Fest. With just one exception, each product in the Neo lineup costs less than $100. That’s still a lot more than a $20 microphone or webcam you could buy on Amazon, but the Neo devices are designed to be premium only at a lower price point. “We have a history of launching products where everybody is like, ‘That’s way overpriced, and I can get this cheaper elsewhere,’” says Fest. “You’re always going to find cheaper options, but I do think we’ve built products here that, for a lot of people, are going to hit that sweet spot.” [Image: The Key Light Neo is very compact and you can wrap the USB cord around the rear. The entire Neo range comes in a white finish, which is designed to blend into rooms with white walls. The compact nature of the Neo lineup also makes it easy to use these devices in smaller spaces or even on the go. All of these Neo products also work on iPad for the first time, a clear invitation to an emerging line of creators that make TikTok and Instagram videos with just their phones or tablets. “We’re able to really accessorize an iPad now and make it a content creation powerhouse,” says Fest. The iPad is often marketed as a creative device, but “the reality of the situation is that the majority of people just use their iPads to watch Netflix and YouTube,” says Fest. Even the Stream Deck Neo will work on an iPad, thanks to a new SDK that will allow app developers to send a profile to the device that lets it control their app. That works around the many restrictions in iOS that don’t exist on Windows or macOS, but it means it will take some time for app developers to build up this support. [Image: The Game Capture Neo can be used on an iPad to capture gameplay. As Elgato looks at new workflows and increased momentum away from being seen as just for gamers, it’s also looking at using AI to make its products even smarter. Fest tells me that Elgato has a new Light Strip launching next month where the 160 LEDs are individually addressable. This is Elgato’s first AI push, with a feature designed to improve how you create a colorful scene. “We built a frontend where you can put in ‘I want a dark forest,’ and on the backend, it will go to ChatGPT ... which will always give us a range of RGB values that serves you three options as a user to pick from,” says Fest. Elgato’s new Prompter hardware is also getting some AI-powered improvements. The teleprompter will soon have voice-based auto-scrolling, making it easy to read off of a script and not have to fiddle with buttons to pause the scrolling. “A few years ago, this would have been a pain in the ass to build,” says Fest, but the availability of large language models has made this a lot easier for the 140-person team working on these products. But for all the advantages of AI, the use cases could eradicate the need for Elgato’s webcams and microphones if the future swings radically toward AI agents that handle our meetings for us. “To some people, that might be appealing, but I don’t think that’s the future I want to fight for,” says Fest. “I think AI can help us in everything we do, and it can make things easier and maybe more fun. It can help unlock creativity, and that’s where we’ll invest and try to build.”

articles.title: Disney Plus is getting another price hike
articles.summary: Disney is raising the price of Disney Plus subscriptions again as part of its mission to squeeze profits from its streaming service.
articles.body: Disney is raising the price of Disney Plus subscriptions again as part of its mission to squeeze profits from its streaming service. The new prices will go into effect on October 21st. The standalone plan with ads will increase by $2 to $11.99 per month, while the no-ads Disney Plus Premium plan will increase by $3 to $18.99 per month (with the annual subscription going up by $30 to $189.99 per year). Various bundles are getting price increases, too, and you can see all of the price hikes on a Disney Plus support page. After launching Disney Plus in 2019 for $6.99 per month, these price hikes are now becoming a seasonal trend for Disney. The company raised the price of its streaming services in December 2022, October 2023, and October 2024, with its streaming business finally becoming profitable for the first time last year. While the latest increases are in line with Disney’s past behavior, the timing isn’t ideal given the PR crisis that followed Disney temporarily pulling Jimmy Kimmel Live! off ABC. Disney announced that the late-night talk show was being restored after having “thoughtful conversations” with Kimmel, just six days after indefinitely suspending production over the host’s comments about the assassination of Charlie Kirk. The decision to pull the show sparked public outrage and calls to boycott subscriptions for Disney’s streaming services. Journalist Marisa Kabas reported on Monday that Disney’s rush to restore Kimmel’s show may have been motivated by the planned Disney Plus price increases. Citing an unnamed Disney source, Kabas said that “with subscriptions hemorrhaging since last week, they couldn’t risk losing more users with this announcement.”

articles.title: YouTube is expanding its AI deepfake detection tool to all adult users
articles.summary: YouTube is expanding its AI deepfake detection program to all users over 18 years old. The tool scans YouTube for deepfakes and allows users to request removals.
articles.body: YouTube is expanding its AI likeness detection program to all users over the age of 18 — meaning just about anyone can have the platform hunt for potential deepfakes of themselves. The likeness detection feature uses a selfie-style scan of a person’s face to monitor YouTube for lookalikes. If there is a match, YouTube alerts the user; the person then has the option to request that YouTube remove the content. YouTube has said in the past that it has found the number of removal requests to be “very small.” YouTube began testing the feature with content creators, and then expanded it to government officials, politicians, journalists, and finally the entertainment industry. The expansion to any user 18 years or older is a significant shift — it essentially gives the average person the ability to constantly monitor content on YouTube that could use their likeness. Takedown requests are evaluated using YouTube’s privacy policy, and the company says it considers removals based on criteria like whether the content is realistic, is labeled as AI-generated, and if a person can be uniquely identified. There are carveouts for things like parody or satire, and the tool only covers facial likeness, not other identifying features like a person’s voice. Users can withdraw from the program and have YouTube delete their data. The news was announced on YouTube’s creator forum, but spokesperson Jack Malon says there are no requirements on what constitutes a “creator” who is eligible. “With this expansion, we’re making clear that whether creators have been uploading to YouTube for a decade or are just starting, they’ll have access to the same level of protection,” Malon said in an email. Deepfake content often centers on celebrities, politicians, or other public figures, but the ability to create a convincing digital replica is a concern for private citizens, too. There have been instances of teenagers being deepfaked by classmates, and three teenagers sued xAI alleging that the company’s Grok chatbot generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM) of them.

articles.title: YouTube will let you ask AI to make a custom video feed
articles.summary: YouTube is launching a new AI feature that creates a personalized video feed based on descriptions of what you want to watch.
articles.body: YouTube is launching a new AI feature that creates a personalized video feed based on descriptions of what you want to watch. In its announcement, YouTube says custom content feeds can be built around your specific interests, moods, or favorite topics, which you can then pin to the top of your YouTube homepage — making it easy to jump back into the feed. This feature is currently rolling out with English language support to YouTube users in the US who are signed in on the YouTube mobile app or desktop. To access it, click on the “Your custom feed” tab at the top of the YouTube homepage and enter a prompt description into the AI text box. For example, you can ask the YouTube AI to “help me unwind with guided meditations under 10 minutes,” or for “deep-dive tech podcasts about AI,” and then receive a curated feed based on your request. It’s similar to other AI-powered feed customization features we’ve seen from other platforms, including Spotify’s prompted playlists. Instagram also gave users more control over their Reels feed algorithm in December, though that uses topic lists rather than descriptive prompts. YouTube says that prompts can be edited at any time to “generate a brand new space” by selecting the text box at the top of your custom feed. To see the “Your custom feed” tab, YouTube says you need to ensure your search and watch history are enabled in your account settings. If the AI messes up your feed request, you can also report the issue to YouTube by clicking the 3-dot menu on the feature tab and selecting “Something wrong?” to leave feedback.

articles.summary: Tech stock news for the week of Sept. 14.
articles.body: Tech stocks fell in early trading on Tuesday, as the AI industry continues to grapple with warnings that the technology could eventually harm humans. The Nasdaq (^IXIC) fell roughly 0.2%.The episode began last week when an Anthropic researcher announced he was leaving the company on X, saying he didn't feel the company was doing enough to keep AI in check.Anthropic Alignment Science Lead Evan Hubinger responded to the post, saying the former Anthropic worker is correct and that he believes there is a greater-than-10 % chance that the technology could "kill all humans."On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei posted an essay responding to the posts, calling on AI companies to slow the pace of frontier AI development. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman agreed.But on Monday's All In podcast, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that the fears of an AI doomsday scenario are simply made up.The various announcements raised questions about whether the AI buildout will continue at its breakneck pace, or if slowing frontier AI models could cut into it.

articles.summary: A continuación puedes comprobar el cupón diario de la ONCE así como los resultados del resto de sorteos de hoy
articles.body: El juego más antiguo de los sorteos de la Organización Nacional de Ciegos Españoles (ONCE) es el sorteo del cupón diario de la ONCE, que ofrece hasta 55 premios que pueden llegar a los 35.000 euros para aquellos que acierten el número de 5 cifras. Junto a este premio se juega 'La Paga', que como su nombre indica, quien se hace con ella recibe una Paga de 3.000 euros al mes durante 25 años si además de acertar el cupón diario acierta el número de serie que acompaña al boleto. El número que ha resultado agraciado con el premio del cupón diario de la ONCE es el: Número de la ONCE: 33548 El número de serie que premia 'La Paga': 032 Los sorteos de la ONCE comenzaron en cada provincia de manera independiente. Su coste solía oscilar entre las 10 y las 25 pesetas. El sorteo entonces consistía en un número de tres cifras y una serie de hasta 5 cifras. En la actualidad, el sorteo de la ONCE ha cambiado, con un número de cinco cifras y tres números para la serie. En 1985 cambiaron los sorteos de fin de semana: el viernes se celebra el Cuponazo de la ONCE, con premios de hasta 9 millones de euros, y el sábado y domingo se juega el Sueldazo de la ONCE, con un premio único de 300.000 euros y una paga de 5000 euros durante 20 años. El sorteo del Super ONCE se celebra cinco veces al día de lunes a domingo. Está organizado por la Organización Nacional de Ciegos Españoles (ONCE). Los sorteos se celebran después del Triplex, cinco veces al día. En la apuesta se seleccionan números en un intervalo de 5 a 11, y podemos escoger desde el 1 hasta el 50. Estos números pueden usarse en un solo sorteo o en varios consecutivos. En los sorteos se extraen un total de 20 números que son los que determinan las combinaciones ganadoras. Los premios del Super ONCE dependen de los aciertos que lleve el participante en su boleto y la cantidad de números que haya apostado. Se obtiene un premio mayor si la cantidad de números apostados y números acertados es similar, es decir, si se apuesta a 7 números y se aciertan los 7, el premio es más grande que si se apuesta por 8 y se aciertan siete. También depende del dinero que se apueste. El premio es mayor si se apuestan 10 euros y se obtienen los mismos aciertos que si se apuestan 5. Los premios pueden consultarse en la web de ONCE. Juega al cupón diario de la ONCE, Super ONCE, Triplex y gana miles de premios. El Triplex de la ONCE es un sorteo que forma parte de la línea de apuestas que ofrece la Organización Nacional de Ciegos (ONCE). El Triplex se puede jugar hasta cinco veces al día y por tan solo 50 céntimos, que es lo que cuesta un boleto. Comprueba en la página web de MARCA si has sido uno de los afortunados en el sorteo del Triplex. Puedes hacerte con premios de hasta 150 euros. El siguiente premio es de 10 euros, si se aciertan las cifras en distinto orden. articles.title: Roku's new Labs hub brings experimental apps to the big screen | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Roku’s latest OS update introduces Roku Labs, a new hub for experimental apps, alongside personalized home screens in more markets, streaming subscription bundles, and more.
articles.body:
Roku is turning your TV into its own testing grounds. On Thursday, the connected TV device maker unveiled the latest update to Roku OS, which introduces a new experience called Roku Labs that allows U.S. customers to access experimental apps made by the company.

These still-in-development apps will be accessible through a new tile on Roku’s Home Screen. Initially, users will see apps for tracking the weather, stocks, and a new game called Roku Dash. The latter involves customers flying a UFO across “Roku City,” the company’s default screensaver of a neon purple and pink city skyline, interspersed with references to pop culture and ads.

The additions suggest Roku is increasing its investment in what could turn out to be monetizable first-party apps that put the company at the center of connected households. Today, the streaming device and TV maker competes with often more advanced AI-powered connected TV products from rivals like Google and Amazon, powered by their assistants, Gemini and Alexa+.

Alongside this update, Roku is making its newer, personalized Home Screen available in new markets, including Mexico and Brazil, where it will offer region-specific features like localized content and tailored suggestions. In addition, Roku’s Voice assistant will now be able to answer weather-related questions.

On the streaming side, Roku will begin offering bundled subscriptions in the U.S. and Mexico that let you mix-and-match streaming plans from smaller services like AMC+, Fox ONE, Hallmark+, Howdy, and Starz. These bundles are usually more affordable than purchasing each plan à la carte.

Roku also said it is open-sourcing the software that powers its Roku remote, Roku LT OS, which could invite outside developers and makers to build their own applications and devices.

articles.title: Lokayukta police trap GST official with Rs 8 lakh bribe
articles.summary: Lokayukta police trap Bengaluru Central GST superintendent accepting Rs 8 lakh bribe via agent; both arrested under Prevention of Corruption Act.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Lokayukta police Thursday trapped a Central GST official while accepting a bribe of Rs 8 lakh through a middleman.GST superintendent Mohit Pratap Singh (south division-4, A-range, south commissionerate), had demanded Rs 20 lakh from a businessman dealing with iron materials to close a case registered against him, according to Lokayukta police. Besides Singh, police also arrested his agent Salman Sheik.“The city-based businessman was booked for evading tax. However, the complaint was false and Singh knew it. When the businessman approached Singh seeking a solution, Singh promised to close the case once for all and demanded a Rs 20-lakh bribe. Finally, Singh agreed to take Rs 8 lakh and directed the businessman to hand over the money to his agent Salman Sheik,” Lokayukta police said.“The businessman approached us and registered a case against Singh and Sheik under the Prevention of Corruption Act. We laid the trap and directed the businessman to hand over the cash to Sheik, who was waiting near Singh’s chamber in Kendriya Sadan, Koramangala. articles.title: Hasan Piker insists Middle East would be 'more stable' if Iran had nuclear weapons during Axios interview
articles.summary: In an interview with Axios, progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker said the Middle East would be "more stable" if Iran had nuclear weapons.
articles.body: Progressive commentator Hasan Piker is not opposed to Iran having nuclear weapons, according to comments he made in an interview with Axios. "Do you think Iran should be free to build a nuclear weapon?" Axios correspondent Alex Thompson asked in a clip that aired Thursday on CNN. "I think Iran, much like any other sovereign nation, has a right to defend itself, regardless of its domestic policies," Piker responded. RADICAL EL-SAYED ALLY DOUBLES DOWN ON ANTI-AMERICAN RHETORIC WITH STUNNING TERRORISM COMPARISON The popular Twitch streamer went on to cite political scientist John Mearsheimer in the belief that "mutually assured destruction is the only way for countries to have sovereignty," something he said would bring regional stability. "Now having said that, do I want Iran to have nuclear arms? No. But I also don't want America, or Russia, or China to have a nuclear arms either," Piker said. "Do you think the Middle East would be more stable if Iran had a nuclear weapon?" Thompson followed. "I believe yes. I think that the Middle East would be more stable," Piker responded. ABDUL EL-SAYED DISMISSES QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER TIES ON 'FACE THE NATION,' PIVOTS TO GROCERIES The far-left personality went on to stress that he's not "advocating" for a nuclear-armed Iran or that it should have weapons-grade enriched uranium, but he insisted that the nuclear conversation is a "distraction." "Time and time again, they have shown, the Iranian government, regardless of whether you want to trust them or not, you can just look at their actions, have proven that they are utilizing the conversation of enriched uranium as a point of leverage to bring America back to the table to get sanctions relief," Piker said. "I do not agree with this statement [on al Qaeda], nor do I give much weight to the statements made by a social media streamer," El-Sayed said. "I am more concerned with the dangerous policies of Donald Trump and Mike Rogers that are raising the prices of gas, groceries and healthcare for Michiganders."

articles.title: El-Sayed tries to put the Hasan Piker debate behind him as midterms approach
articles.summary: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed repeatedly deflected calls to disavow Twitch streamer Hasan Piker's controversial rhetoric.
articles.body: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed has faced backlash for months over his relationship with Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who is known for his controversial rhetoric. The candidate has yet to disavow Piker and now seems to be tiring of the questions, looking to shift focus to the issues that he says are really at the heart of the race. El-Sayed's relationship with Piker was scrutinized before the two of them appeared at a campaign event in April 2026. On March 30, El-Sayed posted a video with the caption "Let's talk about Hasan." In the video, the Michigan Democrat explained that he was looking for a way to access people who "feel locked out of our politics," saying that they are the same people who Piker speaks to through his daily streams. He went on to clarify where he agrees with Piker, which included the streamer's stances on the war in Iran, AIPAC's involvement in U.S. politics and healthcare. "Now, he streams for eight hours a day, every day. A lot of the things that he said, I might not agree with, but that doesn't mean I'm not going to have a conversation with him, and that doesn't mean that the people who listen to him don't deserve to listen to their politicians and to have a pathway into politics to vote for the things that they need and deserve," El-Sayed said. ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK The Michigan Democrat joined "FOX & Friends" ahead of his event with Piker, where he said that appearing with someone did not mean that he agreed with them. While he did not disavow Piker specifically, he referred to the streamer's past remarks, saying, "Of course, I oppose rape. Of course, I don't think 9/11 was justified." Amid the scrutiny of his decision to campaign with Piker, El-Sayed repeatedly blamed the criticism on "cancel culture" and insisted that Democrats needed to be willing to speak with people at their level. The event with Piker went on as planned, but El-Sayed still faced questions. He was asked while standing next to Piker to disavow the streamer's past rhetoric, which he refused to do. "I'm not here to disavow people's views. I'm here to have a conversation about how to get money out of politics, put money back in pockets, and pass Medicare for all. That's the conversation that folks are here to listen to," El-Sayed said in response. EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION The controversy surrounding the April campus appearance would set off a months-long line of questioning, with El-Sayed repeatedly walking the line between condemning some of Piker's rhetoric without going into specifics or alienating the streamer's audience. This became more common after El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., in the Democratic primary in August. Following El-Sayed's victory, Piker called for those who opposed the Michigan Democrat to be "punished" by the party. "You can't be out here saying like, 'Oh, I'm a centrist Democrat. And I think Abdul is a bridge too far.' That must be punished," Piker said. After his primary victory, El-Sayed was asked in multiple interviews to comment on Piker's past rhetoric. When CNN's Kaitlan Collins asked El-Sayed whether he would renounce Piker in August, something that Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., had urged him to do, the Michigan Democrat said he was "less focused on folks who are campaigning with me, more focused on the folks I'm campaigning to." A few days later, El-Sayed was asked about Piker again, this time during an appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press." In response to host Kristen Welker's question, El-Sayed repeated what he said on CNN about focusing more on voters than those who appear with him on the campaign trail. Shortly after El-Sayed's appearance on "Meet the Press," Piker drew the ire of several lawmakers on both sides of the aisle after making a comment that some interpreted as blaming antisemitic attacks on American Jews' support of Israel. "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said during his Aug. 20 stream. HASAN PIKER CALLS FOR DEMOCRATS WHO OPPOSE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO BE 'PUNISHED' The comment set off a wave of condemnations from lawmakers, including Sens. Cory Booker, D-N.J.; Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich.; and Jacky Rosen, D-Nev.; House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y.; and Reps. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J.; Ritchie Torres, D-N.Y.; Jared Moskowitz, D-Fla.; Brad Schneider, D-Ill.; Greg Stanton, D-Ariz.; and Hillary Scholten, D-Mich. El-Sayed issued a statement in which he seemed to distance himself from Piker amid the backlash. "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past," El-Sayed wrote on X. "My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters," he added. "Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk." Shortly after the controversy over Piker's remarks, El-Sayed told Semafor that he had "no plans" to campaign with the streamer. However, this did not stop the press from asking the Michigan Democrat about Piker. During an appearance on "The Breakfast Club" in late August, El-Sayed framed criticism of his ties to Piker as a form of "cancel culture," saying that there was a "massive effort to cancel Hasan." "I think we've got to stop with the cancel culture. It's not about, like, 'Where are you on this one individual?' It's more, 'Do you agree or disagree with the thing that the person said?' And, the thing about it is, that, like, when we play as if the whole person can be reduced to a single soundbite that you took out of context, you're not, you're not dealing with real life," El-Sayed said. ABDUL EL-SAYED DISMISSES QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER TIES ON 'FACE THE NATION,' PIVOTS TO GROCERIES El-Sayed's exasperation with the media's questions about Piker became apparent during a Sept. 13 appearance on "Face the Nation." When CBS News' Weijia Jiang asked El-Sayed about Jewish Michiganders' concerns regarding his ties to Piker, the Michigan Democrat appeared to be fed up. "Weijia, with all due respect, this is the third time you’ve asked about a Twitch streamer in California. I’ve done four events in Michigan this week. You know what didn’t come up? Twitch streamers in California," El-Sayed responded. The candidate said that voters would rather discuss grocery prices, healthcare and the environment, among other things. "I’m not interested in having a conversation about streamers in California because they are not raising the prices of gas and groceries," El-Sayed added. articles.title: Dave Rubin breaks down Hasan Piker's transition from Twitch streamer to political player
articles.summary: Dave Rubin recalls how Hasan Piker rose from Cenk Uygur's The Young Turks to becoming a leading voice among Democratic Socialists on Twitch.
articles.body: Hasan Piker may be a major name in online political media now, but when he got his start at The Young Turks, a network co-founded by his uncle, Cenk Uygur, he was a young, loud guy looking to make a splash in the online political discourse. Dave Rubin, who formerly worked on The Young Turks, recalls Piker as "a big dude" who was "really loud." "[Cenk] just put Hasan on air, even though virtually everyone there wanted to be on air," Rubin recalled in a conversation with Fox News Digital. Rubin said that most of the staff at The Young Turks wanted to be on camera, but "once [Hasan] just showed up, he just got on camera. Cenk just gave him the keys to the kingdom and I guess he became some sort of personality since then." While Piker has continued to profess anti-capitalist and progressive views while building an audience of loyal followers, Rubin later had a political epiphany and realigned himself with the right. In a 2017 PragerU video, Rubin explained that the left had gone from being "progressive to regressive," pointing to cancel culture and calls for censorship, among other things. HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS Rubin said he was not surprised that Piker had gone from Twitch streamer to what he called the "brain trust" of Democratic Socialists. "The Rubin Report" host explained that he saw Piker as filling a void for the left as the right saw a rise in online personalities. Rubin also pointed to the ways in which Piker differed from the typical left-leaning personalities, which he said have made the Twitch streamer resonate with young people. "There weren't that many entertaining new people on the left online. As I said, the right had this rich group of people that was growing and growing and going, whether it was Ben Shapiro or Jordan Peterson or me or Steven Crowder or whoever it might be. There was this long list of people. The left had a couple people…. They were all sort of dorky, effeminate, weird, kind of limp-wristed, low testosterone," Rubin said. "And he came on, and again, he's big, he kind of jacked, you know, he wears his fancy clothes, he is aggressive, it's not really what progressives are," he said. Beyond Piker’s physical presence and media rise, Rubin argued that the streamer's ideology is anchored in an aggressive critique of Israel, something that he said has become more common among left-wing personalities. He argued that progressives "have an endless obsession and hatred of Israel," which he said "is just an extension of hatred of the Jews." FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER EQUATES ISRAEL'S 'RIGHT TO EXIST' TO NAZI GERMANY "You don't have to agree with everything any government does or anything else, but when you have no standards for any other country, and then you hold only one country to any standard whatsoever, and that country happens to be the place where the Jews live, maybe it has a little something to do with Jews," Rubin said. Piker has faced accusations of antisemitism and sparked backlash with a recent comment about Jewish Americans' support for Israel. During his Aug. 20 stream, Piker said, "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews." Several lawmakers condemned the remarks, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y. Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who campaigned with Piker, responded to the streamer's remarks, saying "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence." EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF FROM HASAN PIKER AFTER DISTURBING REMARKS ABOUT JEWISH AMERICANS Rubin believes that one of the reasons behind the focus on Israel is that "Jews don't fit into the intersectional calculator." He said that, while Jews had been historically persecuted, their success in America has made it so they don't fit the mold of an "oppressed minority" the way other groups do. "If you're an oppressed group that's not oppressed, it debunks their whole ideology," Rubin said. According to Rubin, the central hypocrisy comes down to Piker's lifestyle versus the beliefs the streamer professes to hold. This dynamic, Rubin warns, could leave Piker's audience bearing the consequences of his ideas. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "I have no doubt he lives like a capitalist while promoting socialism, and he won't be eaten by the revolution the way some average kid who gets confused by his ideas and then probably gets out there and does something stupid will," Rubin said. articles.title: This little girl grew up with six German Shepherds and thinks they’re her siblings
articles.summary: River grows up alongside six German Shepherds, forming a remarkable bond that turns the dogs into her furry siblings and teachers.
articles.body:
You definitely read about Romulus and Remus, the founders of Rome, who were raised by a female wolf. But have you ever heard of the little girl who was raised by dogs? Well, German Shepherds, at that? Okay, we have your attention now.

Now, the story we're about to tell isn't as dramatic as the intro sounded. But nevertheless, it's bound to bring a bright smile to your face. It's a tale that will warm the deepest and perhaps even the coldest corners of your heart.

And the best part is that it's not even just about the friendship. It's a tale of combined animal parental instinct where a pack of canines takes over the 'duty' of 'raising' a little human. Sounds intriguing? Well, dive right into it.

From the very beginning of her life, River's world was entirely different from that of most children. She did not grow up surrounded only by human toys and traditional toddler routines. No, she was welcomed into a loving pack of six large, majestic German Shepherds. So, in order to ensure everyone's safety and comfort, her parents had taken the introduction process very, very slowly.

For the first few months, a sturdy baby gate kept the curious dogs separated from the newborn. This allowed the pack to safely smell and hear the newest addition to their family. To give credit where it's due, the dogs did an incredible job of remaining remarkably gentle around her. And her parents made sure she was never left unattended with them. With time, the little girl was growing up. And the bond between her and the gentle giants only deepened.

The moment she learned how to crawl, she became the dogs' ultimate shadow. She would follow the pack everywhere around the house, meticulously copying their every move. Her mimicry was so absolute that she genuinely seemed to believe she was just another puppy in the litter.

If her mother wasn't careful, River would sometimes put her hands into the dogs' water bowl and try to drink from it herself. She even tried to eat their dog food! And last but not least, River also loved crawling directly into their large crates to curl up alongside them.

So, River finally transitioned from crawling to walking. And in keeping with it, her puppy-like antics also evolved into mischievous adventures. She quickly became incredibly sneaky around the house. It didn't take long for the clever toddler to observe how the humans interacted with the dogs' enclosures.

One day, her mother caught her figuring out exactly how to open the latches on the dog crates. Armed with this new skill, River took it upon herself to act as the official gatekeeper. She started letting the dogs out whenever she pleased. Whether it was daytime or bedtime, she looked out for her furry siblings, even tucking herself near them to say goodnight before bed.

Among the six German Shepherds, River developed a deeply rooted favoritism for a dog named Roman. Roman was the ultimate big, clumsy goofball and the friendliest member of the entire pack. He took his role as an older brother very seriously, even attempting to gently herd River back toward safety whenever she tried to wander off too far.

When River first started talking, she couldn't quite pronounce the name Roman, so she affectionately dubbed him "Bada" instead. Even now, as a two-year-old who can talk quite well, the sweet nickname stuck, and she still calls her favorite goofball "Bada." She loves him so much that she takes Roman's stuffed animal absolutely everywhere with her.

Now that River has turned two, a beautiful shift has occurred in the household dynamics. She has now confidently stepped into the role of their little caretaker. She actively helps feed them, carefully scooping out the kibble and ensuring it lands safely inside their food bowls. She speaks to them with immense sweetness, gently calling them over and praising them for being "good boys."

River's family has also recently opened up their home to foster rescue puppies. Watching the toddler interact with these vulnerable animals has been incredibly rewarding for her parents. River has shown an innate ability to read canine body language and respect their personal space, making sure never to overwhelm the new rescues. She wins them over instantly by happily handing out treats whenever she can.

Growing up in this unique environment has taught the dogs how to be perfectly calm around children while teaching River invaluable lessons in responsibility, deep empathy, and compassion. Watching their unique relationship develop over time has turned their busy home into something truly beautiful.

Truly, the bond between humans and animals will always remain both heartwarming and mysterious. Nobody can say what exactly causes a particular animal, or in this case, a group of animals, to take a shine to a specific human.

But when it happens, we look upon it with wonder and exclaim out loud with pleasure filling our hearts. We hope that River and her Six Doggos live a great and happy life!

articles.title: All roads lead to cable
articles.summary: ﻿In their fight to win the war for our attention, streamers are re-creating cable from first principles.
articles.body: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on streaming platforms, FAST channels, and the future of entertainment, follow Charles Pulliam-Moore. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started Before Netflix fully committed to becoming a streaming service and leaving DVDs behind, the company experimented with the idea of giving its subscribers a physical box that could access high-resolution digital copies of movies. Films would have been downloaded to the box in the evening and become available to users the next day. But Netflix changed course around 2006 once it saw people were flocking to watch grainy viral videos on YouTube. Though Netflix had already been making waves by disrupting the movie rental business, pivoting to streaming turned the company into a powerhouse that posed a threat to traditional cable services. People loved being able to instantly access large catalogs of movies from their computers without having to sign up for expensive cable plans. Once the company got into original series in 2012, its binge model helped generate buzz and drive new sign-ups. As Netflix’s user base continued to grow in those early years, other companies, like Amazon, Disney, and NBC, realized there was money to be made by launching (or contributing to) streaming services of their own. And while cable didn’t completely disappear as streaming took off, the number of people subscribed to cable plans began (and has continued) to drop over the past decade. How it’s going Streaming is now the most common way that people consume films and television, and many people subscribe to multiple services in order to be able to access all of the things they want to watch. The proliferation of streaming services has led to an explosion of media, but the streaming market’s maturation has also made it much more difficult for companies to find and keep new subscribers. Platforms have tried to get ahead of that issue and stay on top of their finances with countless price hikes that have made it much more expensive to keep up with shows compared to when streamers first hit the scene. In hopes of courting more price-sensitive customers, many companies have introduced ad-supported tiers to their paid services. But some have also launched free ad-supported television (FAST) services that look and feel a lot like traditional cable. Unlike regular streamers where constant ads and endless choices have become an annoyance, FAST services like Tubi, Roku, and Pluto TV keep things relatively simple. In exchange for watching a few commercials, users can browse through entertainment libraries or choose to focus on channels that are dedicated to specific series. When you look at the way that most FAST services present their channels in long lists, it’s easy to get the sense that they’ve been intentionally designed to mimic old cable interfaces. That might speak to entertainment executives beginning to think that icon-dense carousels aren’t necessarily the best way to show off a streamer’s offerings. It could also be a sign that viewers have grown weary of the algorithms streamers use to suggest what content to watch. But it also feels like as the streaming wars have carried on, newer companies realized that the old guard got a few things right. What happens next Because people still want to keep up with all of the new stuff coming out of the paid streamers without having to individually sign up for every service, we’re probably going to see even more bundling in the future. Bundling gives consumers a way to save money on their entertainment budgets, and almost every single one of the major streaming companies has offered some kind of deal that gives you access to one or more of their competitors. Similar to FAST channels, streaming bundles are reminiscent of the tiered cable packages telecoms sell, and some companies, like Verizon and T-Mobile, include access to streaming bundles as perks for their subscribers. More individual streaming platforms will likely roll out always-on channels that are designed to give people a way to watch certain series without having to choose a particular episode for themselves. For services like HBO Max, that would be almost like a return to the way HBO’s various channels air on terrestrial television. In addition to helping viewers deal with decision paralysis, always-on channels could also help streaming services ensure that user engagement stays high. And if every streamer in the game decides that paywalled always-on channels, bundles, and even more price increases are the way forward, it’s really going to feel like we’ve come full circle back to cable. By the way * More streamers have also begun experimenting with vertical content in an effort to meet mobile users where they are. Some of this is a clear response to platforms like TikTok, but it’s also a sign that Hollywood might be serious about getting into microdramas. * Cable prices gradually rose as well, but The Hollywood Reporter has a great breakdown of how much more quickly the cost of streaming services rose. Read this * You should definitely check out The New York Times’ piece looking back on the history of the Cable Center museum in Denver. * Digiday has a great breakdown of just how much more expensive streaming services have become since 2019. * Though many people have fallen out of love with binge-watching, TheWrap has an interesting report about how the model may be coming back into favor.

articles.title: Handcuffed, phones seized: Mumbai student claim cops searched home over pro-Palestine campaign
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Postgraduate student Harshada Borade has alleged that Bandra police's anti-terrorism cell searched her home for over nine hours without a warr.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Postgraduate student Harshada Borade has alleged that Bandra police's anti-terrorism cell searched her home for over nine hours without a warrant and mistreated her friends after she took part in a pro-Palestine kite-flying campaign on Sept 15.Borade said the house owner has since asked her to vacate.Borade, in a video posted on Sunday, alleged that at least 15 cops searched her residence from 5pm on Friday until 3am on Saturday without serving a legal notice or producing a warrant.She claimed plainclothes personnel refused to show identification, forcibly entered her personal space, examined her notebooks and diaries, recorded book titles and photographed and videographed her belongings.Bandra police have not registered an FIR against Borade and are gathering details and conducting a background check on her. DCP (West Zone-2) Mohit Garg said an inquiry was under way "in accordance with procedures established by law".Indian People In Solidarity With Palestine (IPSP), of which Borade is an activist, said six to seven plainclothes personnel identifying themselves as cops arrived at her residence.It alleged that Borade was detained without written notice and later taken back to the residence.IPSP alleged that the search ended after 2.30am on Sept 19 and that Borade's friends were manhandled and abused. It claimed two volunteers were handcuffed, their phones confiscated, and those present threatened with legal action and physical violence.According to IPSP, the panchnama linked the search to a nationwide kite campaign expressing solidarity with children in Gaza. It said the document listed books and quotations by Bhagat Singh and Savitribai Phule among the items found.IPSP also alleged that the panchnama stated the search was not pre-planned but was authorised by senior police officials after personnel found Borade's "behaviour suspicious".You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker lead game-winning drive in OT as Chiefs beat Colts
articles.summary: The Chiefs and Colts played a dramatic overtime game on Sunday night.
articles.body: Last season, the Kansas City Chiefs' magic in close games ran out. It might be back.The Chiefs got a great challenge from the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night. The Colts tied the game late in the fourth quarter and it went to overtime. But Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs' defense had just enough to carry Kansas City to a 33-30 win.The teams traded field goals to start overtime, with the Colts getting one after an apparent game-ending lost fumble by Laquon Treadwell was overturned on a replay review. Indianapolis didn't go for it on fourth-and-8, so that meant Mahomes was getting the ball back with a little more than three minutes remaining, needing just a field goal to win. The Chiefs leaned on Kenneth Walker on the ensuing drive, and a 22-yard pass from Mahomes to Walker got them comfortably into field-goal position. Harrison Butker hit a 40-yard field goal as time expired and the Chiefs improved to 2-0. It was a rough loss for the Colts, who are 0-2. The Chiefs were 1-9 last season in games decided by seven points or less. That came after they won 17 close games in a row, an NFL record. Maybe a new streak is starting. A fun first halfThere were many more points than expected in the first half. A week after the Chiefs' defense did a great job against the Broncos, the Colts were able to sustain drives with little problem. Jonathan Taylor had 75 rushing yards in the first half. Daniel Jones threw an interception that led to a Chiefs touchdown, but he still did enough to keep drives going. Taylor scored on a 24-yard run late in the half to give the Colts a 20-17 lead. The Chiefs were moving it too. Mahomes was sharp, completing 14-of-19 passes for 138 yards in the first half. He threw touchdown passes to Travis Kelce and Xavier Worthy. The biggest miscue the Chiefs had before halftime was a missed field goal. Everything else was smooth. Mahomes was decent last week in his first game back from ACL surgery, and looked a lot more comfortable on Sunday night in Week 2. Both teams looked good. They had 10 combined possessions in the first half, not counting one at the end of the half, and there was only one punt and one turnover. There was certainly some entertainment for the Sunday night audience. That continued through the second half and into overtime. Game remains close in fourth quarterMahomes stayed hot to start the second half. The Colts got a nice tackle on Walker on a third-and-goal run, but the Chiefs went for it and Mahomes found Jalen Royals for a touchdown. Royals had three catches for 9 yards in his career before that play. There might have been some concern over the offseason about how Mahomes would look coming off a major injury, but he has put that to rest early in the season. Even though Mahomes was looking good, the Colts refused to go away. They had some key conversions on a long drive in the fourth quarter and Taylor's second touchdown of the game tied it at 27-27 with 5:37 to go. The Chiefs weren't able to get any points to win in regulation. They had a quick drive and punted after a third-down pass was broken up by defensive back and undrafted rookie Kapena Gushiken, who was pressed into duty due to injuries and made some big plays for Indianapolis. It was the Colts' turn to have a shot at getting the win in regulation. They couldn't come through either. Jones was pressured on a third down and threw it away, leading to a punt with less than 30 seconds to go. The Chiefs couldn't get into field-goal range before time ran out in regulation and the game went to overtime. Mahomes made the first big play of overtime with a 30-yard pass to Tyquan Thornton on third-and-12. Kelce picked up another first down to get the Chiefs into field-goal range. The drive stalled and Butker got a field goal for a 30-27 lead. The ensuing drive seemed like it might last one play. Treadwell made a long catch but got up for extra yards and had the ball punched out. It was ruled a fumble, but the turnover call was overturned on replay once it was shown that Treadwell was being touched when he had control of the ball and then went down to the ground. Indianapolis retained possession but couldn't score a game-ending touchdown, settling for a tying field goal. Mahomes had a lot of time. The Chiefs started the drive slowly and then Walker broke a 22-yard catch to put Kansas City in position to win. As he has done many times, Butker finished the win with a field goal.

articles.title: Giants vs. Rams live updates, news, inactives: Puka Nacua ruled out, Aaron Donald comes out of retirement to make 2026 season debut
articles.summary: The Rams host the Giants to close out Week 2 on Monday Night Football.
articles.body: The New York Giants and Los Angeles Rams are set to close out Week 2 on "Monday Night Football" tonight, coming off drastically different season openers. The Giants started the 2026 season red-hot under new head coach John Harbaugh, steamrolling the Dallas Cowboys in primetime with an incredible performance from second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart. He fired on all cylinders in Week 1, completing 79.3% of attempts for 230 yards, 3 touchdowns, and 0 interceptions while adding another 54 yards on the ground. The team also saw star receiver Malik Nabers make his return from a torn ACL, reeling in 69 yards on six catches Despite entering the year as heavy Super Bowl favorites, the Rams started the season appearing sluggish, dominated by the San Francisco 49ers in the league's first regular-season game in Australia. Myles Garrett failed to register a single tackle in his debut for the team after a blockbuster trade from the Cleveland Browns this offseason before electing to undergo knee surgery for a nagging injury that clearly bogged him down in Week 1. articles.title: WWE Raw results, grades (Sept. 21): Penta wins chaotic MITB qualifier after Solo Sikoa abducted mid-show
articles.summary: "WWE Raw" returned to San Antonio with a chaos-filled show capped off by Penta's surprise Money in the Bank qualifier win.
articles.body: "WWE Raw" returned to San Antonio's Frost Bank Center this Monday, Sept. 21, after a fantastic evening last week in Mexico City. This week's show was a proper follow-up, setting the table for an exciting immediate future.😱 Abduction of the Night!So, this is the most perfectly "wrestling thing" ever. We can't really get into the meat of this episode without starting with a literal abduction.It all centered around 946, who are suddenly the serious version of the old, questionably themed tag-team Cryme Tyme. If you know, you know. Since their big debut as a trio, Royce Keys, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price have done next to nothing of substance other than perform backstage attacks or film "warning" videos — until tonight, when they literally abducted Solo Sikoa mid-show, effectively removing him from his Money in the Bank qualifier match in the evening's main event.WHAT JUST HAPPENED?!?!? 😱Solo Sikoa has been TAKEN!!! pic.twitter.com/goDZBxaN8p— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 Now, this is admittedly really dumb. There's no good reason for Keys, the source of this stable, to be pursuing Sikoa and/or LA Knight other than sheer pettiness. The whole genesis of his issues were from the freaking Bloodline, so why he isn't specifically targeting them is beyond me — but it's now bringing the Bloodline, Sikoa and Knight together in a loose, unexpected way.Unless 946 gets a few more additional members, they're foolishly setting themselves up for a three-against-six war if you include Roman Reigns. Internet chatter suggests Jacob Fatu is secretly aiding 946, but may I remind you that he was the one who put Keys out in the first place.Does that mean it won't happen? No. Would that make it make sense? Also definitely not. Therefore, it's entirely possible.Things are as complicated as ever in The Bloodline! 🩸@jacobfatu_wwe | @WWEUsos pic.twitter.com/k2CnEQAx2w— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑We might as well segue right to it before the main event chatter, but Knight is still immaculate when given an uninterrupted time slot to speak.Tonight, "The Megastar" delivered a vintage, passionate promo that gave me some (probably foolish) belief that he very well may pull off a title win over Reigns at Money in the Bank. He even addressed exactly what I just alluded to, which was a great touch. He's been a voice for everything fans have thought in recent years. And while I have lost all hope, I'll still be wildly thrilled if WWE actually pulls the trigger..@RealLAKnight WANTS to be acknowledged as the NEW World Heavyweight Champion! 🙌Will he get it done at Money in the Bank? pic.twitter.com/OHf7XHXWxd— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 As for the Sikoa relationship, it's nice to see them staying aligned as buddies. The Money in the Bank mention was well played — until it didn't matter, thanks to 946.YEAH 🗣️@RealLAKnight pic.twitter.com/2lvRb7Kb0Z— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 Penta in the BankIn the end, Penta replaced Sikoa and then beat Dominik Mysterio and Dragon Lee in a phenomenal main event. This triple-threat match was a certified banger and delivered some seriously clever near-fall spots. Two of them came from Mysterio hitting 619s out of nowhere. Who knew that move could even be done like that?HOW did Dirty Dom execute that counter?!? 🤯@DomMysterio35 pic.twitter.com/1ZZ46E2SpI— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 THIS MATCH!!! 🤌 pic.twitter.com/DvAd4bJR1B— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 It was a great match, and it came after Penta opened the night with a big presentation before fending off Mysterio and JD McDonagh. Penta stayed focused on Reigns and the world title, which makes me think he might be the one to win it all at Money in the Bank. A Penta cash-in would be a pretty perfect way to kickstart a likely short title reign, but a fun one nonetheless. The dude is a star.Penta QUALIFIES for Money in the Bank!!!! 👏@PENTAELZEROM pic.twitter.com/pWajRBL6DR— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 Penta gained the respect of the ENTIRE WWE Universe last week in Mexico City! 🔥@PENTAELZEROM pic.twitter.com/b9hfAM8OIf— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 Penta gets the better of BOTH Dirty Dom and JD! 👊@PENTAELZEROM pic.twitter.com/6jzLtqk5Qy— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 Roxy's RoadWhat do you know? WWE is going a fresher route with many of the entrants in the upcoming ladder matches, and Roxanne Perez added her name to the list by beating Iyo Sky and La Catalina in the women's Money in the Bank qualifier.Admittedly, coming into it this grouping felt like a great way to tease Perez and Catalina's upcoming title match at WWE x AAA Worlds Collide this Saturday, while still giving Sky the win. But nope. Perez scored a clean pin over Sky with a Pop Rox after a very solid, interference-free match. (Because Judgment Day never helps Perez.)ROXANNE 💪@roxanne_wwe QUALIFIES for Money in the Bank! pic.twitter.com/jGeKGy3BJz— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 Despite WWE's wealth of great options to win the women's ladder match in New Orleans, this could — and arguably should — be used as the vehicle to finally break up Judgment Day. At the very least, separate Perez from the group after winning and have Liv Morgan's jealousy get the best of her — or have Perez potentially cash in on Morgan if she ends up regaining the gold. There are plenty of options right now, which is always a good thing.Did you know this show has tag-team champions?You really would never know that "Raw" has tag-team champions. Because it essentially doesn't. Bron Breakker has completely separated himself into his own primary quests while, for some unknown reason, hanging onto a belt alongside Austin Theory. He's pursued Oba Femi and a world title while still being a tag-team champion. They haven't even defended the tag titles since recapturing them against the Street Profits.Honestly, just get rid of them, WWE. We know how much you don't care.And to prove it, Breakker had an "impromptu" match with Je'Von Evans that stunningly ended via a typical Vision DQ. I'm not sure what's more annoying between Vision or Judgment Day interference.OBA!! OBA!! OBA!! 👑@Obaofwwe wipes out the ENTIRE Vision!! pic.twitter.com/cS3ZEmG1Kk— WWE (@WWE) September 22, 2026 Either way, it was all to continue the Femi feud and tease a pairing with Evans. If we really get a tag title match between Femi and Evans against the Vision out of this, it would actually be hilarious. Especially if Femi wins tag gold before going after that title shot he won through the King of the Ring.Wherever this ends up going, you'd best bet your bottom dollar Femi shows up in that Money in the Bank match to stop Breakker."Raw" has some good momentum right now. articles.title: Hasan Piker admits he has 'dialed down' his opinions after public and Democratic backlash
articles.summary: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker told Jon Lovett that he has toned down his rhetoric amid backlash, but his controversial remarks continue to roil Democratic campaigns.
articles.body: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker admitted on Friday that he has "dialed down" his commentary since facing backlash for taking part in Democratic candidates' campaigns. Piker discussed the ongoing controversy surrounding his past statements with "Pod Save America" co-host Jon Lovett, particularly after his Axios interview last week in which he described America as "pound for pound" worse than al-Qaeda on terrorism. The progressive commentator argued that many of his comments are taken "out of context" or taken from a longer statement but added that, more recently, he has begun to think about what he says and tone down his rhetoric. HASAN PIKER SAYS HE’D ‘ABSOLUTELY’ CAMPAIGN FOR AOC IN 2028 AS EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF "There’s also the third thing, which is like actual positions that I hold, actual opinions that I have that are unbelievably antagonistic to those in positions of power, that when they hear that, they like lose their minds," Piker said. "They don't know how to deal with it. And when I'm faced with a question like that, I have to in my mind make this calculation of: Should I be honest about what I believe? Should I take a principled stance on something, or should I portray myself as a campaign surrogate and act as though I am running for office?" He continued, "And I've definitely dialed down. I know it doesn't seem like it. And I've definitely dialed down my commentary with that in mind for sure." Piker did not clarify what opinions he has softened but suggested that the backlash against him is largely because Republicans "don't really have a good midterm message." "Just because it's their most successful narrative doesn't mean that it's going to be successful in winning elections for them. And I don't think it will be successful in winning elections for them at all," Piker said. FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER CALLED OUT BY MS NOW HOSTS IN FIERY EXCHANGE OVER HIM BEING A DRAG FOR DEMOCRATS He added, "Because look, I've gone all up and down the country. I have fans in many places all around this beautiful country. And you know, there's obviously a lot of Republicans that don't like me and maybe even some liberals that don't like me, but by and large, the idea that a Twitch streamer is supposed to be held to a higher standard than the president is such an insane phenomena that it could only be concocted by a bunch of out-of-touch people in mainstream outlets that think this is a salient narrative that will definitely work because people don't care." Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment. Piker has garnered nationwide attention after campaigning with Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed during the primary election. Since winning the Democratic primary, El-Sayed has attempted to distance himself from Piker, repeatedly referring to him as a "streamer from California" with no relevancy to the race despite their multiple past appearances. OCASIO-CORTEZ CALLS FOCUS ON HASAN PIKER 'ABSOLUTELY LUDICROUS' AS SOME DEMOCRATS DEMAND DISTANCE Other Democratic figures have largely come out against Piker as he continued to make controversial comments, such as suggesting that Jewish Americans were bringing violence upon themselves based on their support for Israel. Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin himself distanced his party from Piker and his "deplorable" comments during an interview with Fox News Digital on Tuesday. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Let me just say that I think it's absolutely disgusting and deplorable the things that Hasan Piker has said," Martin said. "But he does not represent the Democratic Party, and he certainly doesn't represent the viewpoints of almost every one of our candidates and our elected officials."

articles.title: YouTube is building AI creator tools that do almost everything for them
articles.summary: YouTube has steadily added more and more AI-powered creator tools that do everything from generate thumbnails to offer script feedback.
articles.body: Part of the job of a content creator is to figure out how to get their work in front of the most people. Cracking — or fighting — the algorithm has historically been a frustration for creators, but YouTube is increasingly simply telling creators what they should do. At the annual creator-focused Made on YouTube event, the company announced updates to the suite of AI-powered creator tools it unveiled in 2025. In its initial iteration, the dashboard of creator tools included things like A/B testing for video thumbnails and a chatbot interface to query how content was performing. This year’s update adds AI tools for more complex tasks. Perhaps most significantly, YouTube is introducing an AI “agent” that will work in the background to optimize a creator’s channel. For example, the tool will monitor a creator’s back catalog of videos, looking for content that has taken on a new life, is relevant to the news, or has started trending. The agent will offer suggestions for tweaking the thumbnails or titles for older videos to ride the new wave of relevance. The tool can also put together things like pitches for brands by combing through a creator’s YouTube channel and pulling out demographic and audience data to make a case to potential sponsors, says Amjad Hanif, vice president of creator products at YouTube. [Image: Creators can ask YouTube’s built-in AI tools for video feedback. The new features iterate on previously existing AI-powered tools. The agent will now generate entire thumbnails and titles based on the content of an uploaded video, and creators can ask the tool for feedback on their own thumbnails. Viewers may also see different content as creators run tests via YouTube Studio: A dynamic thumbnail tool allows creators to upload up to three different images for each video, and YouTube’s system will assign the best one to different audience segments to try to boost watch time. YouTube is taking it a step further, too, by allowing creators to test three different versions of videos — a clip with a different intro and hook, for example, or with a different structure — to see how each performs. The different versions of the same video will be fed to small audience segments to test which results in the highest watch time; creators can go forward with the “winner” to make it the permanent video, or YouTube will automatically do so after seven days. Hanif says the YouTube system ensures the three video versions are not “dramatically different” from one another. How content creators use AI has been a hot-button issue in some circles. Earlier this summer, Hank Green angered fans when he acknowledged that he had been relying on AI to do research for his videos. (Some observers diagnosed Green’s problem as not one specifically about AI, but rather about overwork and burnout in the creator industry.) It’s not just Green who’s had to defend himself: There are countless stories of brands using or promoting AI — or simply being suspected of doing so — that have spiraled into scandal. For many content creators or public figures, using AI in their work is a reputational risk; is using YouTube’s behind-the-scenes AI tools something they’re worried about? Hanif differentiates between instances where creators are using AI to be more efficient, versus when the tools are doing the actual job of a creator. “What I’ve heard from creators and what I’ve seen from my own conversations with viewers is that when it feels like it’s not actually from the creator, but the tools have taken over and the tools are producing the content, I think that’s kind of where it crosses the line a bit,” Hanif says. Writing the script, shooting the scenes, wholesale creating the content — these are the types of AI use that might become a problem for creators and viewers, he says. The real question is what tangible effects this suite of AI tools actually has on creator success. Have views exploded for YouTubers doing A/B testing? Does using the chatbot to plan or tweak content help creators connect more with what their audiences want to see? I asked YouTube and Hanif if they had data that shows the tools actually improving metrics for the creators who use them, but the company declined to share anything. What it does do, per Hanif, is save creators time. “The time that we’ve saved there is time that goes back into the creativity,” Hanif says.

articles.title: Disney+ and Hulu add to the growing trend of streaming inflation | TechCrunch
articles.summary: At the same time, Disney appears to be exploring new ways to expand its streaming business beyond simply raising subscription prices.
articles.body:
Streaming is getting more expensive again. Disney is the latest media giant to raise prices for its streaming services, adding to a growing pattern across the industry. The increases come roughly a year after Disney’s last major streaming price hike .

Disney is raising the price of its ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle to $21.99 a month, up from $19.99, whereas the ad-free stand-alone plans are each rising to $21.49 per month, up from $18.99. The company is also increasing the price of its stand-alone ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu plans to $12.49 a month.

The new prices are reflected on Disney+’s support page . Bloomberg was the first to report the changes.

Disney+ and Hulu are hardly alone. Streaming companies have spent the past several years steadily increasing prices. Peacock and Apple TV also raised prices in August, while Netflix increased prices earlier this year.

When Disney+ launched in 2019, its basic monthly subscription cost $6.99. Since then, the service has gradually moved further away from that intro price as Disney has tried to turn streaming into a profitable part of its entertainment business.

The latest increases come as streaming remains an increasingly important part of Disney’s overall business. In its third-quarter 2026 results , Disney said entertainment streaming revenue from Disney+ and Hulu rose 11% to $5.5 billion, driven by subscriber growth and the impact of previous price increases.

At the same time, Disney appears to be exploring new ways to expand its streaming business beyond simply raising subscription prices.

The company has reportedly explored the possibility of introducing a free tier for Disney+. This could put the company in more direct competition with platforms such as YouTube and Tubi, which have been capturing a growing share of consumers’ viewing time.

Earlier this month, Disney+ also introduced “ Playlists ,” a new feature designed to help users discover and continuously watch curated selections of content.

The company is making changes on the technology side as well. Disney recently hired Karandeep Anand as its first-ever chief technology officer. Anand is the former CEO of Character.AI, a company Disney previously accused of infringing on its intellectual property.
